explanation: This pole is a sequence-opening detector with no lexical trigger of its own: it sits at full strength on a text's first token whatever that token is (the protocol's first-token floor - 0.96-1.01 for every first token tested except the bare digits 1-9), and once the text has real context it is silent (98.8% of the 199,636 scanned mid-document tokens are below 0.05 of the 1.5 peak, and only six reach 0.4). The one consequence the measurement can see is that a prompt opening with a bare numeral gets that opening response one token late, on the first token after the digit run - '8 people...' peaks on ' people' (0.99), '17 March...' on ' March' (0.98), '28/11/2011' on '/' (0.96) - whereas the identical words after a letter, punctuation mark or CJK character leave the measured peak at or below 0.14.
